Unexpected certificate warnings or changed gateway MAC addresses

Alerting on certificate anomalies, DAI violations, and unexpected ARP changes

SSH and management over encrypted channels

Valid HTTPS makes silent interception and modification much harder

Isolate the attacker, reset exposed credentials, and strengthen Layer 2 defenses

Using TLS with strong configurations and current protocol versions

A surge in certificate warnings or DAI violations

Verifying host key fingerprints helps detect impersonation

Connecting through a VPN and verifying server identity

Enable DHCP snooping and Dynamic ARP Inspection

Using SFTP or FTPS instead of plain FTP

Attackers may alter data in transit, so integrity checks and encryption matter
Which control helps verify that a downloaded file was not modified in transit?

An on-path attacker may forge DNS responses, so DNSSEC and encrypted DNS help

Encrypting signaling and media with SRTP and TLS

Endpoint tools that flag gateway or certificate anomalies aid detection

Enforcing MFA and resetting exposed credentials

Managed devices with VPNs and certificate validation resist interception better

A traceroute showing an abnormal extra hop on a local path

Isolating guests limits an attacker's ability to intercept internal traffic

Managing trusted root CAs and removing untrusted ones

Combining Layer 2 protections, encryption, validation, and monitoring is most effective

Verifying the site's valid TLS certificate and using HTTPS
